pool.text: Sebastián de Belalcázar came to the American continent in the third voyage made by Columbus.
Sebastián de Belalcázar joined Francisco Pizarro in the conquest of Peru after serving in Darién and Nicaragua.
Sebastián de Belalcázar separated from Pizarro's expedition to find the city of Quito.
Petecuy formed a large army with many tribes and fought the Spaniards on Holy Tuesday.
The Spanish explorer Sebastián de Belalcázar founded Santiago de Cali.
Captain Miguel Muñoz moved Santiago de Cali to its present location under the orders of Belalcázar.
Belalcázar moved the governing function of Cali to Popayán owing to better weather.
Santiago de Cali had thousands of inhabitants, including a population of African slaves.
Soap Varela Hermanos was created during the early industrial growth period.
Cali ceased to be a single point of trade and its economy focused on industry.
Army trucks filled with dynamite exploded near the train station and destroyed city blocks.
The Cali Fair began to be celebrated as the most important cultural event.
Santiago de Cali hosted the Pan American Games and was named the Sports Capital of Colombia.
The government of Cali inaugurated La Torre de Cali, the city's largest building.
Mayoral elections started in the municipality of Cali.
A notable cultural building containing exhibition saloons and a cinema was restored.
The national government could not respond to local politicians as an economic crisis became apparent.
The Masivo Integrado de Occidente public transit system began operations in the city.
Ciudad Delirio premiered as a feature film set in Cali centered on salsa dancing.
Cali became a focus center of Colombian protests marked by deadly clashes.
